## Recursive string methods
---
Let's write a method that returns t/f if a char is in a string
v1:
```
public static boolean findChar(String word, char target) {
	if(word.length() == 0) {
			/* Since we searched the entire word and found nothing, we 
			/* can safely return false
		return false;
	} else if(word.charAt(0) == target) {
		return true;
	}
	
	// Pass in substring of word, except the first letter
	return findChar(word.substring(1), target);
}
```
But in this version we are wasting data, so we will use indices instead now
v2:
```
public static int findCharIndex(String word, char target, int index) {
	if(index >= word.length()) {
		return -1;
	} else if(word.charAt(index)) {
		return index;
	}
	
	// DON'T use incremental op index++, will cause stack overflow
	// Since it's after the var it uses the index first THEN updates it
	return findCharIndex(word, target, index + 1);
}
```

## Recursive math
___
Now let's calculate a sum with recursion, where we want to add all numbers from `start` to `end` inclusively.
```
public static int sumRecur(int start, int end) {
	if(start == end) {
		return 0;
	}
	
	returns start + sumRecur(start + 1, end);
}
```

This method will print out the list of even numbers from `start` to `end`.
```
public static String getEvenRec(int start, int end) {
	if(start > end) {
		return "";
	}
	if(start % 2 == 0) {
		return start + " " + getEvenRec(start + 1, end);
	} else {
		/* Don't need to concatenate, already did in the previous
		iteration */
		return getEvenRec(start + 1, end);
	}
}
```

## Recursion over array
---
When given an array or reference type of any kind, we need to be careful to not destroy the data unless explicitly told to.
```
public static boolean find(int[], nums, int target) {
	return findAux(nums, target, 0);
}

// Using an aux method to not destroy data
public static boolean findAux(int[] nums, int target, int index) {
	if(index >= nums.length()) {
		return false;
	} else if(nums[index] == target) {
		return true;
	} else {
		return findAux(nums, target, index + 1);
	}
}
```
